title: Shortpatch autosuggester and safe executor for admin fixes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: On-call engineers repeatedly perform small, high-value fixes during incidents (ACL tweaks, cache clears, routing weight adjustments). These short fixes are currently documented in disparate runbook snippets and hand-run scripts which produce poor telemetry and inconsistent audit trails. Goal: deliver an "autosuggester" that reads incident context + telemetry, proposes 1-3 safe shortpatch actions ranked by confidence, and can execute a vetted action under strict safety gates (dry-run, RBAC scope check, approval flow). This ticket covers the prototype orchestration, safety gate designs, audit telemetry contract, and an initial CLI/web action executor that integrates with existing runbook fragments.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype autosuggester returns at least one ranked suggestion for 80% of sampled incident contexts (internal test harness)
Each suggested action includes: human-readable intent, required RBAC scope, estimated blast radius, and dry-run output if applicable
Executor supports: dry-run, staged apply (canary), and full apply with approval step; all executions emit structured audit events to admin-telemetry
Safety gates verified: RBAC enforcement, non-production guard, and approval enforced for high-blast actions
Integration tests + a lightweight canary run on the ops-lab cluster before rollout

2025-03-01: Implemented dry-run plumbing and audit event emitter; initial end-to-end test against a dev cluster passed (non-destructive actions only)

comments: PM (Aisha Patel): We must avoid over-automation for high-blast actions. Keep default to suggestion-only unless explicitly allowed in team config.
Security (Jonas Meyer): Audit payload must include pre/post snapshots and operator identity; include correlation_id to incident timeline.
Design (Priya Rao): Suggestion card should show last-time-this-fix-was-applied and owner/maintainer link for accountability.
SRE (Carlos Vega): We should add a throttling policy when autosuggester triggers during high-alert floods to avoid noisy fixes.
tasks: Write suggestion schema + confidence buckets and store in schema-registry
Add dry-run path that returns simulated side-effect logs
Wire audit events to admin-telemetry with correlation_id
Create approval UI hook for console and CLI
Add idempotency token and optimistic lock in executor
E2E tests against ops-lab cluster and runbook snippet corpus
Prepare rollout plan and 2-week canary runbook
risks: Accidentally enabling destructive fixes without explicit approval could cause customer impact
Autosuggester confidence calibration may overfit common incidents and miss novel failure modes
Telemetry/visibility gaps could make it hard to debug why a suggestion was chosen
Concurrency issues when multiple operators try to apply the same fix during an incident
decisions: Decision: Suggestions are default read-only; execution requires explicit opt-in per team and explicit approval for high-blast actions
Decision: Use existing admin-telemetry event schema v1 with added fields rather than create a new telemetry stream
Decision: Initial suggestion scoring will be a lightweight rules+feature hybrid (heuristics + simple ML score) to keep iteration fast
Decision: Executor will validate RBAC via the central authz service; deny-by-default if scope missing
